# Flow: SQL behind a page (SQL button / right-click -> /api/sql -> page_sql)

One-line summary: the top-bar "SQL" button or a right-click on the page opens `SqlPanel`, which asks `GET /api/sql` with the current page and its params; `server.sql_page` returns `access.page_sql()`: commented read-only queries over `SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE` with the SET lines filled in, from the `access_queries/` files (`query_file`) or the app's own text (`plain`, `activity_section_sql`). Each query shows in a `SqlBox` with a copy button. On the Activity tab every section also has its own SQL button, fed by `section_sql` in the `/api/activity` answer. The app never runs this SQL.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as User
    participant AP as App.tsx
    participant SP as common.tsx SqlPanel / SqlBox
    participant S as server.sql_page
    participant A as access.page_sql
    participant F as access_queries/*.sql
    U->>AP: click "SQL" or right-click <main> (Shift + right-click: browser menu)
    AP->>SP: SqlPanel(page, params + view)
    SP->>S: GET /api/sql?page=...&user|role|name|show...
    S->>A: page_sql(page, p)
    alt show=activity
        A->>A: activity_section_sql per section key (ACT_BASE + ACT_FILTER + ACT_SECTIONS), query_sql
    else grants / tags / rules
        A->>F: query_file(file, title, SET values)
        A->>A: plain(title, about, sets, body)
    end
    A-->>S: [{title, sql}]
    S-->>SP: {page, queries} (None dropped)
    SP-->>U: one SqlBox per query (Copy SQL); Escape or Close hides it
    Note over U,SP: Activity tab: Sec sql=key -> SQL button -> SqlBox(section_sql[key])
```

## Steps

1. `App` keeps `sql` state for the panel — `web/src/App.tsx:266`. The top bar has a "SQL" button that sets it — `web/src/App.tsx:325`. A right-click anywhere on `<main>` does the same and suppresses the browser menu unless Shift is held — `web/src/App.tsx:332`.
2. While open, `SqlPanel` renders at the top of `<main>` with `page = loc.page` and `params = {...loc.params, view}` — `web/src/App.tsx:333`.
3. `SqlPanel` calls `useApi("sql", {...params, page})` -> `GET /api/sql?...` (inside Snowflake the same call goes through the st_react bridge, [streamlit-in-snowflake.md](streamlit-in-snowflake.md)); Escape closes it — `web/src/pages/common.tsx:111-114`, `web/src/api/client.ts:69`.
4. Route: `GET /api/sql` -> `serve("sql")` -> `ROUTES["sql"] = sql_page`; not in `WITH_REFS`, so no `refs` — `server.py:2386-2388`, `server.py:2271-2273`, `server.py:2277-2284`.
5. `sql_page(p, view)` returns `{page, queries}` = `a.page_sql(page or "home", p)` without empty entries — `server.py:1697-1699`.
6. `page_sql(page, p)` picks names from `user` / `a`, `role`, `name` / `obj` / `table`, sets the activity window, and builds the list per page ([logic/page-sql.md](../logic/page-sql.md)) — `access.py:4471-4558`:
    - `show=activity`: warehouse -> QUERY_HISTORY by warehouse + `5_object_users.sql` (`access.py:4478-4485`); otherwise one `activity_section_sql` per section plus `query_sql` (`access.py:4486-4492`);
    - user / role / object: `query_file` on `2_user_access`, `1_user_roles`, `3_role_access`, `4_role_holders`, `5_object_users` with `USER_NAME` / `ROLE_NAME` / `OBJECT_NAME` set, and tags and policies on the object (`access.py:4493-4520`);
    - usage, sensitive / flow / review, rules / home / whatif / review and the fallback add their own `plain` queries (`access.py:4521-4557`).
7. `query_file` reads `access_queries/<file>` and rewrites its `SET` lines with `lit()` values; inside Snowflake the files are on the app stage from `PUT_QUERIES` — `access.py:4377-4386`, `sql/4_streamlit.sql:45-46`.
8. The panel shows a header (read-only, change the SET lines, run with your own role, the app never runs them), a Close button and one `SqlBox` per query: title, Copy SQL (`copyText`, "Copied" or "Select and copy"), and the SQL in a `<pre>` — `web/src/pages/common.tsx:115-121`, `web/src/pages/common.tsx:98-107`.

### Per-section SQL on the Activity tab
9. `activity_page` adds `section_sql = {key: activity_section_sql(name, what, first, last, key).sql for key in ACT_SECTIONS}` — `server.py:1687`; type `ActivityPage.section_sql` — `web/src/api/types.ts:1257`.
10. `Activity` puts it in the `SectionSql` context — `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:70`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:112`.
11. `Sec` reads its `sql` key from the context; when there is text, a SQL toggle button sits next to the section's own controls and opens a `SqlBox` above the section body — `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:73-83`. Keys used: off, touched, hours, objects, client, kinds, matrix, type_day, by_day, who, ddl — `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:270`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:370`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:398`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:449`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:515`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:538`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:568`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:637`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:671`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:707`, `web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:135`. The `tiles` key is in `section_sql` and `page_sql` but no section card uses it.

## Example (fake data, `test_server.test_sql_page`, `test_server.py:657-675`)

| Request | Answer holds |
|---|---|
| `/api/sql?page=access&role=F_ANALYST` | `SET ROLE_NAME = 'F_ANALYST';` |
| `/api/sql?page=object&name=SALES.CORE.TBL_CUSTOMER` | `SET OBJECT_NAME = 'SALES.CORE.TBL_CUSTOMER';` |
| `/api/sql?page=access&user=O'BRIEN&show=activity` | `SET USER_NAME = 'O''BRIEN';` |
| `/api/sql?page=home` | `SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE` |
| `/api/activity?name=SALES.CORE.TBL_CUSTOMER` | `section_sql` keys include client, kinds, matrix, type_day, by_day, who, hours, off, touched, ddl; `hours` holds `$TZ_HOURS` |

Every answer: starts with a comment, reads ACCOUNT_USAGE, no write keyword outside comments — `test_server.py:670-673`.
